sections.kicker: Prepared for KLYR by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: KLYR has a distinct color world. The site first screen does not say what the product is.
sections.keep: Your grid. Each bottle sits against a bold flat color, and you recognise it as KLYR before reading the name.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The bio is a pun on the name and says nothing about the product.
pins.why: A stranger cannot tell it is a bottle, nor that it has swappable lids.
pins.how: Add one line that says what KLYR is, then keep the pun.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: The wordplay is read by people who already know you.

pins.quote: Our interchangeable lids keep your KLYR dressed for every mood.
pins.what: Your real difference sits in one caption.
pins.why: Lids you change are why KLYR and not another bottle on the shelf.
pins.how: Make the lid idea the first thing the brand shows.
pins.label: Your captions
pins.cost: Visitors see another bottle in good colors.

pins.area: Orange centre panel reading FUN between two cropped product close-ups
pins.what: The first screen says fun and shows no bottle.
pins.why: Close-ups of lids and an engraving do not tell a first visitor what KLYR makes.
pins.how: Show the whole bottle and say the idea in the headline.
pins.label: Your site
pins.cost: A visitor from Instagram does not recognise the product they saw.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at KLYR. I spent some time on your site and your Instagram. Three things stood out.
